newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIA SEMIS-Tight spreads negate upgrades.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIA SEMIS-Tight spreads negate upgrades.

text.p: Australian semi-government yields followed government bonds lower over the last week, but the news of two states being placed on review for a ratings upgrade had little impact because spreads to bonds are currently tight.
The decision by the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee not to lift interest rates last week, and continuing speculation of another local easing has underpinned local debt markets.
While short end spreads narrowed after holding reasonably steady over the previous couple of weeks, spreads at the long end widened for the second consecutive week.
Traders said there was a bit of volatility in the margin to bonds, with spreads both widening and narrowing during the week.
"There was a lot of interbank-type activity, spreads were in and out on the day depending on the flow versus bond," one trader said.
The states of Victoria and West Australia, and their respective semi-government debt, were placed on review for upgrade by Moody's Investor Service on Friday.
Traders said the news had little market impact, mainly because spreads to government bonds were already very tight and, in the case of Victoria mainly, an upgrade had already been factored in.
"Everything's trading so flat on the credit band anyway that these announcements have no effect anymore," the trader said.
"In the old days when something was 40 over the other it did mean something," he said.
"But given that most semi-governments trade almost flat to each other now, there's very little reaction, or there's no reaction basically, on credit upgrade announcements," he said.
Offshore, New South Wales Treasury Corp (T-Corp) tapped the Eurobond market with a A$200 million issue. The three year bonds pay a semi-annual 6.0 percent coupon and issue price was 99.052.
Queensland Treasury Corp (QTC) issued a 30 billion yen yen/Australian dollar dual currency samurai. Priced at par, the two year bonds carry a 5.5 percent coupon.
There were no domestic tenders last week, and traders do not expect one this week.
The last tender was held by QTC on September 19.
In other news, Treasury Corp of Victoria has finalised the consolidation of the July 2000 stock into five other lines.

When TCV announced the restructuring of its debt earlier this month, it said once the consolidation was complete it would be looking to issue a new 7.50 percent August 2008 stock before the end of the year.
